one_liner: Lead a shift in the Capitol Police's 24/7 Protective Intelligence Operations Center, triaging threats against Congress and coordinating partner agencies and emergency response.
fit_summary: The posting requires 52 weeks of GS-12-level experience leading 24-hour protective or intelligence shift operations and analyzing threat investigations. Daniel's emergency planning and exercise work touches continuity, but his resume shows no watch-center, protective or threat work, so he likely won't qualify.
eligibility: Open to the public, and U.S. citizenship is required; no federal status is needed.

You need at least 52 weeks of specialized experience at the CP-10/GS-12 level covering all four areas: leading 24-hour protective or intelligence shift operations, coordinating information and reports on investigations, analyzing alleged threats, and briefing senior leadership and external stakeholders.
Education cannot substitute for experience at this grade.
You must pass a full field background investigation and all pre-employment evaluations, then complete a one-year probationary period.
You must be available for all three shifts (0600-1400, 1400-2200, 2200-0600), including nights, weekends, and holidays.
keywords: federal, state, and local partner agencies
strategy: First, honestly test yourself against all four specialized-experience elements. If you cannot point to at least a year of leading 24/7 shift operations and threat analysis, consider skipping this posting or targeting entry-level USCP or intelligence-analyst roles.

Answer the KSA narratives and questionnaire honestly and back every 'expert' rating with a concrete resume example. USCP evaluates quality, depth, and complexity, and inflated ratings can be caught during review.
Emphasize interagency coordination with federal, state, and local partners and any briefings you gave to client leadership.

The announcement opens October 29 and closes November 12, 2026. Submit several days early, and have your references and background-investigation history (addresses, employers, foreign contacts) ready.
resume_bullets: Led a Simulation Cell unit at FEMA full-scale exercises two years in a row, delivering notes used for the after-action reports.
Facilitated full-scale and tabletop exercises for federal, state and private-sector clients (2022–2024).
interview_questions: Describe a time you were the senior person on duty and had to make a fast call on an emerging incident with incomplete information.
How would you triage several incoming threat reports at once, and how would you decide who to notify?
Tell us about briefing senior leadership or partner agencies on a sensitive operational matter.
How do you supervise and hold accountable a mixed team of employees and contractors across rotating shifts?
watch_outs: The specialized-experience bar is high and narrow, and his resume shows no 24/7 protective or intelligence operations.
The job requires rotating shifts with overnight, weekend, and holiday work, has no telework, and means a commute from Manassas to Capitol Hill.
The application window is only two weeks (October 29 to November 12, 2026).
